h: Timing Your Throw on a Big Cardiff Weekend
p: Cardiff is a city that comes alive when there's a match or a gig on, and St Mary Street is right in the middle of it. That's brilliant for atmosphere but it does mean planning ahead. If there's a rugby international or a big concert at the Principality Stadium, the whole centre fills up, so book your oche well in advance and give yourself extra time to get through the crowds. On quieter weeknights, it's a far more relaxed affair, which can suit a work social or a smaller group better.

A tip for groups: decide before you arrive who's in charge of picking the games. Flight Club has a mix of formats, and having one person steer the evening keeps things moving and stops the night turning into a debate. Starting with something simple and working up to the more chaotic games is usually a winner.

Before or after, there's plenty to explore. Cardiff Market, the Victorian indoor market just off St Mary Street, is great for a browse and a bite. Bute Park stretches out behind the castle and is lovely for a walk, especially on a sunny afternoon. The National Museum Cardiff, in the civic centre, is free and packed with art, natural history and dinosaurs. And Cardiff Bay, a short hop away, has the Wales Millennium Centre and the Senedd on the waterfront.
Put all that together with a few rounds on the oche and you've got the makings of a proper weekend in the Welsh capital.
